The implementation is complete and the full test suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 1 test — the sole test class; the other files are the base/helper classes).

## What I changed

In `OwnerRestControllerV1.java`, the business-day rule for `registrationDate` previously only rolled weekends forward to the following Monday. I extended `toBusinessDay(...)` to also roll past the fixed public-holiday list:

- Added a `PUBLIC_HOLIDAYS` set with the five listed dates: `2026-01-01`, `2026-01-26`, `2026-04-25`, `2026-12-25`, `2026-12-28`.
- Rewrote `toBusinessDay` as a forward-rolling loop that advances one day at a time while the date is a weekend **or** a public holiday, stopping on the first non-holiday business day.
- Extracted an `isWeekend(...)` helper.

The loop (rather than a single switch) correctly handles chained cases — e.g. `2026-12-25` (Fri) rolls Sat 26 → Sun 27 → Mon 28 (holiday) → **Tue 29**, and the Saturday holiday `2026-04-25` rolls straight through the weekend to the next business day.

This preserves the existing behavior (`resolveRegistrationDate` still writes the adjusted date back onto the request, and the daily-limit counting continues to key off the adjusted date), while satisfying the acceptance invariant that the default `registrationDate` is never a Saturday or Sunday — and now never a listed holiday either.
